name: Anuj Kapoor

thesis.text: I go where technology is rewriting economics and markets,

strap: Right now that means making a forest as legible to markets as a bond, putting Himalayan supply chains on digital rails from loom to London, threading solar energy systems with a distributed platform, and building digital intelligence that lets a small team move at the scale of an institution. Trained as a banker and technology strategist, wired as a founder, and drawn into policy and advisory because the future needs better rules, I spend half my time thinking ten years ahead and the other half building towards it.
workNote: Open to partnerships built on shared value.

tile.title: About me
tile.teaser: Venture and product builder, asking one question for twenty years.

panel.title: How economics changes when technology arrives

blocks.text: One question has run through my career: how does economics evolve when new technology arrives?

I trained in classical economics and business, then went to the LSE to study the future of technology at the dawn of social media, and what it would mean for social and economic systems. I then spent eight years inside the machinery of capital, structuring cross-asset derivatives at Citigroup and investments at EFG Private Bank.
In 2011–12 Satoshi Nakamoto's paper made that question real: an information system redesigning money, trust and institutions. I left banking in 2012 to follow it.

Since then the pattern has repeated. Find the shift early, learn its economics, technology and incentives properly, then put it to work: in a Himalayan village, at a London market stall, in a carbon registry, inside an AI system, and in policy.
Deep multidisciplinary rather than a generalist: I go far enough into each field to build something that works, then connect it to everything else I know.

blocks.text: My partner is a software consultant, and we live between London and Shimla.

Many of my creative ventures began by connecting back to home and family. Himalayan People started as a way to work with and support communities close to where I was born, and Festival People is a game I designed so we could celebrate festivals together from wherever we were.

items.title: Open to
items.text: Advisory, board and strategy roles where something new needs to be understood, then built.

blocks.text: I do my best work where the value we create together is the point. I'm most interested in partnerships, equity or shared-upside arrangements, and long-term collaborations, where reward follows the value created rather than time billed.
If you're building something worthwhile and prefer to work that way too, I'd be glad to hear from you. The email address is at the top of the page.
